newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended firm on Tuesday, hitting new record closes on good local and offshore demand as confectionary and snacks firm Afbrand soared to a 226 close from its 100 cents issue price, dealers said.

"We are closing looking good, almost at day's highs. There is no real fundamental reason apart from what seems to be...movement from bonds into equities," James Scott, an equity marketing manager at stockbrokers Societe Generale Frankel Pollak told Reuters.
Dealers said the market was still looking for an interest rate cut before the end of the year.

They added that a weaker rand, orbiting at six-month lows against the dollar, was having limited negative effect on sentiment as the industrial index rocketted 73.0 points to a new all-time closing high of 9,183.2.
The all-share index ended up 47.4 points to a record close of 7,492.6.
"The rand is really behaving as anticipated. It's been weakening in the face of a strengthening dollar," Scott said.
"A slightly weaker rand is probably not a bad thing in terms of giving some support to the gold producers and some of the other exporters," he added.
But bullion's slide to weaker levels as it lost support at $323.00, added to the gloom in the gold shares. The gold index finished down 15.9 points to 954.0 points.
Platinum stocks rekindled interest on a higher white metal price and Implats and Leplats added 25 cent and five cents to finish at 50.75 rand and 490 cents respectively.
Leplats earlier hit a new 12-month high of 505 cents.
Dealers said overall volumes were good, averaged at around 800 million rand on the day.
In the broader market advancing issues led declining issues by 212 to 152, while 29 shares surged to new highs and 17 shares sank to new lows.
Dealers said the market would continue firm on Wednesday.
"On the equity market the outlook and the undertone remains positive," one Johannesburg Stock Exchange dealer said.
Electronics firm Daewoo tumbled after issuing a warning of a half-year loss in its earnings. The stock finished down 68 cents at 230 with volumes at 2.3 million rand.
Chemicals firm Sentrachem finished up 208 cents to 10.00 rand on interest after Dow Chemicals made an offer to buy the group at a price of 10.50 cents a share.
Dealers said good institutional buying fuelled near-dated South African share futures to also finish higher.
The September industrial contract was last at 8,665/70 from 8,601 settlement, the gold contract at 665/70 from 685 settlement and the all-shares contract at 6,699/710 from 6,668.
